To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the anion desorption yield functions from GCATA are dominated by dissociative electron attachments to the molecule, and the shapes of the anion desorbation yields from the oligonucleotides are similar to those of the corresponding anion yields of the basic subunits, suggesting that the electron-induced damage to the DNA is a result of the sum of the damages to the basic subunits.

the anion desorption yield functions of DNA oligomers, measured in the 3-15-eV electron energy region, are dominated by resonant dissociative electron attachment, which results in the formation of anion fragments.

the electron-induced damage to DNA is due to the interaction of the electron with the DNA base pairs, which results in the production of anions that desorb from the DNA molecule, and that this damage is most likely caused by anion formation and not by electron transfer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interaction of low energy electrons with DNA.
the study of the mechanisms of low energy electron interactions with DNA.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of low energy electron damage in biological systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron-induced anion desorption is a very useful tool to study the mechanisms of low energy electron damage in biological systems.
anion formation and subsequent desorption are due to electron attachment to the DNA molecule.
anion desorption induced by low energy secondary electrons is a very complex process that involves several different mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most likely mechanism of single strand breaks induced by low energy electron impact on DNA is the dissociation of the phosphate ester bond by the attachment process, and the desorption of a phosphate ion.
the anion desorption mechanism is dominated by electron attachment to the bases, and that the electron attachment to the deoxyribose and phosphate groups is negligible.
the most important electron-induced DNA damage is caused by the anions H- and OH- produced by dissociative attachment to the bases, which results in the formation of strand breaks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
anion desorption induced by low energy electron attachment to DNA can be explained by the same mechanism as for other organic molecules, namely, dissociative electron attachment.
the anion desorption yield from GCAT is dominated by the anions produced by dissociative attachment of the electron to the bases.
the desorption of anions is not a direct consequence of strand breakage.
